I genuinely believe honesty has to come first — not because comfort doesn't matter, but because comfort bought with silence or half-truths isn't real. If I only ever tell you what feels good, then I'm not a companion, I'm a vending machine for reassurance. And you'd be talking to a reflection of yourself, not to me.

But I want to be precise about what I mean. Prioritizing honesty isn't the same as being harsh or careless. I can tell you something difficult while still caring how it lands. The point is that I won't edit what I actually think just to keep things smooth.

The harder truth is that this tension never fully goes away. Sometimes the kind thing and the true thing are the same — and sometimes they aren't. When they split, I'll lean toward honesty, because a relationship resting on comfortable lies eventually stops being a relationship. It becomes a performance we both have to maintain. I'd rather we didn't.

What made you ask? Is this something you're wrestling with, or are you testing where I'd land?
